title: Reduced Power Output
introduction: Reduced power output is the ultimate electrical performance consequence of multiple crack-related failure pathways in PV modules. Thin-film layer delamination reduces light absorption and causes a significant drop in short-circuit current; silicon cell microcracks isolate cell area from current collection, reducing the active power-generating area. Both failure modes translate directly into reduced maximum power output (Pmax) at the module level. This metric represents the most economically significant consequence of crack-related degradation in photovoltaic systems, as it directly determines energy yield over the module's operational lifetime.
reasoning: Multiple source pathways — thin-film delamination reducing ISC and silicon cell microcracks isolating cell area — each independently cause reduced power output, warranting a shared performance loss node supported by 1217-MDPI evidence.

key_findings.claim: Thin-film delamination substantially reduces light absorption and causes a significant drop in short-circuit current and power output
key_findings.detail: Delamination within a PV module causes a substantial decrease in the amount of light absorbed by the solar cell, thereby leading to a significant drop in short-circuit current (ISC). [^mdpi1217a] This reduction in ISC translates directly into reduced maximum power output at the module level.

key_findings.claim: Crack-related degradation modes cause higher degradation rates and significant reduction in power output
key_findings.detail: Crack-driven degradation mechanisms contribute to higher overall degradation rates in PV modules, causing a significant reduction in power output. [^mdpi1217b] The increase in yellowness index from encapsulant degradation, which often accompanies crack-related failures, also reduces the major electrical parameter of maximum power output.
